artboards.title: As it stands today — seven panels, none ranked
Proposed — the finding that is worth the most, open
Proposed — three findings open: a panel, a chart, and the quadrant
Proposed — nothing found, nothing judgeable, and a failed read

annotations.text:
THE JOB OF THIS SCREEN

Analysis is seven panels stacked in a column, all the same weight, none ranked. Its own header admits the problem: "read this when you have a question, not every morning." A screen you only open with a question in hand is a screen that never tells you the question you should have asked.

You settled four things in the interview and everything here follows from them.

1. IT LEADS WITH WHAT IT FOUND, RANKED BY MONEY. Not seven panels. A queue of findings, ordered by what fixing each is worth, so the top three are the answer and you can stop there.

2. A PANEL BECOMES A FINDING. Nothing is deleted. Each of the seven panels is now the EVIDENCE inside a finding -- the table, the chart, the arithmetic -- and it only appears at all when it has something to say. A quiet week is three rows, not seven empty boxes.

3. THE SENTENCE COMES FIRST, THE CHART ON DEMAND. You told me you want "cash out has beaten cash in three weeks running, 2.4m net" rather than a bar chart to read. So the finding says that in words and money, and the chart lives inside it as the thing that proves it.

4. IT IS A DESK SCREEN. The phone is a competent reading fallback -- the position, the findings, the figures -- not a second full design. No scatter plot, no charts, four cards and the count of what is below.

Everything is drawn from index.html's own values: the 23-colour palette, the 11/12/13/14 ramp, Inter + Archivo Black + IBM Plex Mono, and the .ow-* console components already shipping on Today, Debtors, Chase debts, Follow-ups, Consignment, Creditors and Pricing. No new colour, no new weight, no new type size, no fourteenth button family.

WHAT IS WRONG WITH IT AS IT STANDS >
The eight circles on the artboard.

1. A 140-CHARACTER PARAGRAPH, UNMEASURED, OPEN ON EVERY VISIT. Seven screens already put the long version behind the "i" bubble and keep a one-line sub. This is one of the ones left.

2. ONE WINDOW GOVERNS SIX PANELS AND IS IGNORED BY THE SEVENTH. Prices To Check deliberately ignores the date range -- correctly, a price does not stop being stale because you were looking at last quarter -- but it says so in the fourth sentence of a paragraph nobody reads. The control and the exception are 1,800px apart.

3. SEVEN PANELS, ALL THE SAME WEIGHT, NONE RANKED. This is the fault the other seven are symptoms of. Asked which of the old dashboard's panels they read, the owner said "honestly, I stop at the top" -- and this screen is what the bottom half became. It kept the shape that caused the problem.

4. TWO CHARTS TO BE TOLD ONE THING. Units and revenue side by side, and the finding is the GAP between them -- which is the one thing neither chart draws. You are asked to do the subtraction by eye, weekly, across two grids with different scales.

5. FOUR SERIES COLOURS -- ONE OFF-PALETTE, ONE IS THE ACCENT. The quadrant paints #3B82C4, which is not one of the 23. It also paints a group in oxide, the accent that is meant to appear ONCE per screen as the thing to do next. A scatter plot's whole point is that POSITION carries the meaning; four fills on top of position is decoration that costs the screen its accent.

6. BADGES THAT SAY "GOOD" ABOUT THINGS THAT ARE NOT. Iron sheets keeping 9% -- your thinnest big line -- wears the same green pill as PVC pipe keeping 31%, because the badge is green whenever the field exists. Next to it, Bugolobi's 1,910,000 is badged green for being 22 days old while a smaller, older debt is badged red: the colour is reading the age and ignoring the money.

7. A 500-CHARACTER PARAGRAPH ABOVE THE MONEY IT EXPLAINS. Prices To Check has the best writing on the screen and puts all of it before the table, unmeasured, on every visit.

8. NO PANEL SAYS HOW MANY ROWS IT CUT. Every table is a silent top-5 or top-8. Only Prices To Check ever says "N more", and only when you scroll past it. The app's own law is that a truncated list names what it dropped.

THE PROPOSAL -- what changed, and why

THE STRIP IS THE POSITION; THE QUEUE IS THE FINDINGS. Five figures that answer "where do I stand" -- what you kept, what you are owed, whether cash is running down, what is standing still, and what the list below is worth. Below it, six findings ranked, and one row that is not. The last tile does NOT add the queue up, because the queue holds two kinds of money: it carries the yearly total and the one-off total as two figures. A single number there would have broken the screen's own rule on its most prominent tile.

THE HARD PART, SOLVED IN THE OPEN: TWO KINDS OF MONEY IN ONE ORDER. A margin you lift comes back EVERY MONTH. Cash you are owed, or cash locked in stock, comes back ONCE. They are not the same money and nothing on this screen ever adds them -- so every row's basis line says which it is ("a year, if you lift it" / "owed, once" / "locked up, once"), the ranking is done on one stated clock (worth over a year: a month's money twelve times, a one-off once), and the rail says so in those words. That is why 985,600 a month sits above 2,480,000 in Kato's account, and you can disagree with it because it is written down. This is the same discipline Pricing already uses for thin lines against dead stock.

THE ROW IS 44px AND CARRIES WHY IT IS WHERE IT IS. Name, the finding in one clause, the reason, then the figure and its clock. The reason column never truncates; the name gives way -- except in the evidence tables, where the item name IS the identity and the supplier gives way instead.

COLOUR ONLY WHERE IT MEANS SOMETHING. The old screen badges every row. This one has two state colours on the whole desktop: the net-cash tile, because cash genuinely running down is bad news, and "96 days" on Kato, because that threshold is genuinely crossed. Everything else is ink. The ranking already says which is worst; a chip on every row would say nothing.

THE ACCENT APPEARS ONCE, INSIDE THE ONE OPEN FINDING. One oxide button, on the one thing to do next. Every other action on the screen is a ghost.

FINDINGS CAN POINT AT EACH OTHER, WHICH A PANEL SCROLL CANNOT. Open the margin finding and it tells you the buying price behind it is 94 days old -- lift against a cost nobody has confirmed since June and you are guessing at the very number you are correcting. That amber line is finding 1 warning you about finding 2. Seven separate panels have no way to say that.

THE ACCOUNT OF WHAT WAS READ. 412 items read, 7 findings, 398 with nothing to report, 58 judged by nothing because they have no cost on file. This is the only device that lets a reader trust a list for what it does NOT say, and Pricing already proved it is the best thing on a screen like this.

HEIGHT: the old screen is roughly 2,600px of panel. The position, all seven findings, one of them fully opened with its arithmetic and its evidence, and the account, now fit above 1,030px.

CASH IS NOT IN THE RANKING, AND THAT IS THE POINT. "2,440,000 net out" is an eight-week running total: neither a month's money twelve times nor a one-off, so it has no honest place on the ranking's clock. Putting it fifth by size would have been a second, unstated rule on a list whose whole claim is that its order can be checked. It keeps its row, its sentence and its chart, under a hairline reading POSITION, NOT A FIX. It is the thing the other findings explain, not another thing to fix.

THE ARITHMETIC IS THE DELIVERABLE, SO IT HAD TO SURVIVE BEING CHECKED. Every figure now derives from the one under it: 704 sheets at 45,400 against a 41,200 cost keeps 2,956,800; the same 704 at the 12% rule's 46,800 would have kept 3,942,400; the difference is 985,600 a month and 11,827,200 a year, which is what the row says. The five evidence lines total 87,083,600 of the window's 148,600,000, so they fit inside it. The eight stale prices total 3,720,000, which with the six held back at 400,000 is the 4,120,000 the row claims. And the account partitions what was read: 412 items = 354 with nothing to report + 58 that nothing can judge.

The rule on roofing is 12%, not the 22% first drawn. No wholesaler holds 22% on plain iron sheets, and a target the shop could never hit would have made the biggest finding on the screen wrong in the direction that flatters it.

THREE FINDING KINDS -- and where the old panels went >

Three findings are open at once here so the shapes can be compared. In the app one is open at a time.

THE PRICES FINDING IS THE OLD PANEL, INTACT. Same ordering, same reasoning, same honesty -- and now with the paragraph AFTER the row that summarises it rather than before the table it introduces. The "6 more, worth 400,000" line and the "6 of 20 checked, and this undercounts rather than flatters" line both survive, because they are the two best sentences on the current screen.

THE CASH FINDING IS THE ANSWER TO YOUR THIRD QUESTION. You said you want the sentence, not the chart. So: "cash out has beaten cash in for three weeks running, 2,440,000 net out." Open it and there is the arithmetic on the left and, on the right, the eight weeks as NET -- in minus out, one bar per week, one colour meaning good and one meaning bad. The old grouped-bar chart made you subtract sixteen bars by eye to see the thing the chart existed to show. This draws the subtraction.

AND THE LINE THAT MATTERS MOST IS THE FOOTNOTE: "cash in is money that ARRIVED, not sales made. A strong week sold on credit shows here as nothing." The current screen never says this anywhere, and without it the panel is genuinely misleading in the one month it matters.

AND THE QUADRANT, WHICH YOU SAID YOU READ. It is the evidence inside "four lines nobody has bought in 90 days". Same plot, one change: position already carries the meaning, so only the corner this finding is ABOUT is coloured, and the four dots in it are named on the chart rather than in a legend beside it. The four-colour legend is gone -- it spent the screen's accent on a chart series and put an off-palette blue next to it, and it was explaining a thing the axes already say.

Beside it, the four lines and what each is holding, and the consignment warning: six of the eight wheelbarrows are somebody else's, so clearing them below 104,000 comes out of your own pocket. That is the same distinction Consignment already draws, brought to the screen where the decision is actually made.

WHAT I HAVE NOT DECIDED FOR YOU

1. THE RANKING CLOCK. A year: a month's money twelve times, a one-off once. It is the honest way to put two kinds of money in one order and it is written on the screen so it can be argued with. If you would rather cash you can collect always led -- money in the drawer beats income on paper when you are short -- that is one comparator and one sentence in the rail.

2. THE THREE PANELS YOU DID NOT PICK. Cash bridge, demand trajectory and demand breadth are not deleted; they are findings that appear when they have something to say. Cash is drawn here. Demand trajectory has no finding on this artboard because I have not decided what its threshold IS -- "a gap opened between units and revenue" needs a number before it can rank, and that number is yours. Say it and it becomes an eighth finding.

3. "NOT NOW" NEEDS A RULE. Every open finding offers it. I have not decided whether dismissing hides it for a day, a week, or until the figure moves. Until the figure moves is the honest one, but it means a finding you dismissed can come back the same afternoon.

4. THE BADGE ON THE RAIL IS 7. One screen, one number, and it counts findings. If you would rather it counted only the ones worth over some amount, that is a real choice about what the badge is for.

5. WHAT I HAVE NOT TOUCHED: dashboardContext and the arithmetic behind every figure, priceReviewCandidates, the going-quiet rhythm calculation, the CSV, or renderDashboard's call into this. This is a design, not a rewrite -- the same seven readings feed it.

6. THE OLD NAMES stay as search keywords: analysis, charts, trends, margin, quadrant, demand breadth, cash bridge, leakage, quiet, prices to check.

THE THREE STATES A SCREEN IS ONLY DESIGNED ONCE YOU HAVE DRAWN >

NO STRIP OF ZEROS. Five tiles reading 0 fills a healthy screen with figures that mean nothing and makes a good month look like a broken app. The settled state carries three real figures instead -- including THE THINNEST LINE YOU SOLD, which is the one reading of "nothing to fix" worth anything: it says how close the bar came to catching something. 19.4% against an 18% rule means the screen is working, not asleep.

"NOTHING TO FIX" AND "NOTHING THAT CAN BE JUDGED" ARE DIFFERENT SCREENS. The second one is 147 lines -- more than a third of the month -- sold with no cost behind them. The shop cannot say what those kept, and reporting "nothing found" over that much of a month is a lie by omission. So it is a finding in its own right, about the books rather than the trade, and it names the door that fixes it.

THE THIRD STATE DOES NOT EXIST TODAY. If the sales ledger fails to read, the current screen shows the same empty panels a quiet week shows, and those two are not the same news. The app's own law says a failure must name itself: so it says what failed, when the last good read was, that those figures are NOT shown because a figure with no date is worse than no figure -- and it still shows the ONE finding that does not come from the ledger, because stale prices are true whatever the ledger is doing.

EACH OF THESE IS A WHOLE SCREEN, so each carries its own single accent. That is two oxide buttons on this artboard -- one each on the two screens that have something to do. The settled state has none, because when nothing is wrong there is no next thing.

THE PHONE -- a reading fallback, and honest about it >

You said Analysis is a desk screen you rarely open on a phone. So this is not a second full design competing with the desktop; it is the same findings, readable in one hand, drawn from scratch at 390 rather than reflowed.

820px is a switch: 44px navy bar, 26px Archivo page name, 15px card titles, 14px padding, cards instead of 44px rows, a white 60px tab bar with the active tab FILLED rather than merely coloured. No fake status bar and no fake keyboard -- the real ones render on top of this.

WHAT IS DROPPED, DELIBERATELY: every chart, the quadrant, the arithmetic, the evidence tables and the rail. A scatter plot at 390px is a smudge, and the reasoning behind a finding is desk work. What survives is the two things a phone is for here: where you stand, and what the list says.

THE STRIP IS 2x2 IN ONE CARD with hairline dividers and no per-tile border, which is the house pattern.

THE ACCENT IS ON ONE CARD, NOT ALL FIVE. A button on every card is five oxide buttons on a screen allowed one. It sits on the top finding, because the list is ranked and the top of it IS the thing to do next.

AND THE LIST ACCOUNTS FOR ITSELF: "2 more below, 3,390,000 between them." A phone shows fewer rows than a desk; it must say so, and say what it is holding back.
